question.worked_solution:
We use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1\,⟹\,1-{cos}^{2}⁡x={sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{2{sin}^{3}⁡x}{1-{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\frac{{sin}^{3}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /4} \\  & =-2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})] \\  & =-2\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$
